name: UpsellPlus
summary: Upsells, cross-sells and free gifts across Shopify product pages, cart, checkout, post-purchase, customer accounts and POS, with AI recommendations and A/B testing in 23 storefront languages.
best_for: shopify merchants who want one app covering product page, cart, checkout, post-purchase, customer accounts and POS offers rather than three, especially Shopify Plus stores, where the checkout half of the product actually works
skip_if: your upsell revenue sits near the $500 ceiling that Free and the $49 plan share (the first paid step buys features, not headroom) or you are not on Shopify Plus and were buying this for the checkout upsells
honest_knock: The plans are capped by the revenue they are allowed to earn you, and the first paid step does not raise that cap: Free and the $49 Launch plan both stop at $500 of upsell revenue a month. The $49 buys offers and features, not headroom: headroom starts at $119. And crossing a ceiling is not something you decide: their FAQ says you are automatically upgraded to the next tier so the offers keep running, so a good week moves the invoice on its own. Read the feature list closely too, because the tier named Shopify Plus is not the same thing as the requirement: their FAQ says Plus is needed only for checkout customization and checkout upsells, so on a standard Shopify store the checkout half of a checkout-upsell app is not what you are buying. The last thing to know is at the top, and it is not on their pricing page. The plan card says Scale stops at $5,000 a month while the comparison table on that same page says Unlimited; we asked, and UpsellPlus support confirmed on 21 September 2026 that Scale is a revenue ladder - $199 up to $5,000 of upsell revenue a month, $299 up to $10,000, $399 up to $15,000, $499 up to $20,000, $699 up to $30,000, $799 up to $40,000, and an Unlimited plan at $999 with no ceiling - and that passing $5,000 moves a store to the $299 tier on its own. That is better news than the Enterprise tier above it suggests, but it means the number you are quoted at signup is the floor of a ladder whose higher rungs are not published anywhere.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Basic · per month, or $500 a year
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/upsellpluscheckout and in our own test that day; earlier: listing and vendor pricing page re-verified 2026-09-19 on apps.shopify.com/upsellpluscheckout, USD; the Scale ladder confirmed in writing by UpsellPlus support on 2026-09-21) Fixed monthly tiers based on the revenue generated through UpsellPlus offers, with no percentage commission. The listing shows four: Free runs one offer, opens all twelve upsell types plus analytics, and allows up to $500 in upsell revenue. Launch is $49 a month or $500 a year (saves 15%) and allows the same $500 of app-generated revenue a month, adding cart, pop-up and drawer upsells, product page and post-purchase upsells, multivariate A/B testing, progress bars and free gifts. The tier named Shopify Plus is $119 a month or $1,149 a year (save 20%), raises the ceiling to $2,000 a month and adds checkout customization, checkout upsells, thank-you page customization and AI recommendations. Scale is $199 a month or $1,899 a year (save 20%) for up to $5,000 a month, live support and multivariate A/B testing. 14-day free trial on the paid tiers; charges billed every 30 days. The vendor's own page adds two things the listing does not carry: a fifth Enterprise tier with no published price, sold through a demo, and a Managed Service at an extra $499 a month. That page contradicts itself on Scale - the plan card and the listing both say up to $5,000 a month, while its comparison table puts Scale under Unlimited - so we asked the vendor. UpsellPlus support answered on 21 September 2026 that Scale is a ladder rather than a single price: $199 up to $5,000 of upsell revenue a month, $299 up to $10,000, $399 up to $15,000, $499 up to $20,000, $699 up to $30,000, $799 up to $40,000, and an Unlimited plan at $999 with no ceiling. A store that goes past $5,000 is moved automatically to the $299 tier, which covers up to $10,000. So the plan card is the accurate one and the comparison table is wrong, and the amounts above $199 appear nowhere on the published pricing page (figures from UpsellPlus support, 21 September 2026). Hitting a ceiling is not a stop: their FAQ says you automatically upgrade to the next tier so upsells are not interrupted, so the bill rises by itself. Their FAQ also states Shopify Plus is NOT required except for checkout customization and checkout upsells, which is a Shopify restriction; cart, product page, cart drawer, thank-you and post-purchase offers work without it. Read again on 17 November 2026: the listing (4.9 stars is not stated; it shows 5.0 from 151 reviews) now names the plans Free, Basic $49, Pro $119 and Advanced $199 a month, the tiers we recorded as Launch, Shopify Plus and Scale, each paid plan with a 14 day free trial, and its Free card now reads “Build for free. Launch with a free trial” without the $500 ceiling it carried before. In our own test the same day the app showed no Free plan: on our Shopify development store its billing page said the store had full access to every feature, free, and that development, partner and Shopify staff stores are never charged, so no Shopify approval screen appeared. Its “How pricing works” table followed the upsell revenue the app generates: Basic $49 up to $500, Pro $119 up to $2,000, Advanced $199 up to $5,000, then the steps the vendor's support gave us in September, Scale 1 $299 up to $10,000, Scale 2 $399 up to $15,000, Scale 3 $499 up to $20,000, Scale 4 $699 up to $30,000, Scale 5 $799 up to $40,000 and Unlimited $999. The listing shows tiers only up to $199, so the app's table is the first public place the higher steps appear. The app called the entry plan Basic, not Launch. We could not test the listing's Free plan on a development store.

schema_offer.description: Basic, per month, or $500 a year; capped at $500 of app-generated upsell revenue a month (the entry plan was called Launch until November 2026). Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-17.

compare_with.name: AfterSell
compare_with.why: Both are Shopify upsell apps and both are strongest around the checkout. AfterSell is the tighter, better-known post-purchase and checkout play; UpsellPlus spreads wider: product page, cart drawer, checkout, post-purchase, customer accounts and Shopify POS in one app, with 23 storefront languages and integrations into Klaviyo, Recharge, Appstle, Skio and Smartrr. The catch is the revenue ceiling on each UpsellPlus tier, so compare on the plan you would actually need rather than on the entry price: free and $49 stop at the same $500 a month.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested UpsellPlus on a Shopify development store: the install without a payment or approval screen, one Smart cross-sell play for the cart drawer with 10% off that gave a preview about 4 minutes and about 6 clicks after the install click (The Inventory Not Tracked Snowboard $949.95 to $854.95, Gift Card $10.00 to $9.00), the Billing page with nine revenue steps from Basic $49 to Unlimited $999 a month, and the uninstall, which asks for a reason. Nothing was saved or published and no order was placed, so no shopper data was seen. Name: the listing (apps.shopify.com/upsellpluscheckout) is titled UpsellPlus Checkout Upsell, developer UpsellPlus, Built for Shopify, rating 5.0 from 151 reviews, and matches the dossier; the app opens as UpsellPlus. The listing says Free plan available. Free trial available. and shows a plan box with Free (Build for free. Launch with a free trial, Choose from all 12 upsell types, Checkout Upsells (Plus only), Analytics), Basic $49 (up to $500), Pro $119 (up to $2,000) and Advanced $199 (up to $5,000), each with a 14-day free trial. Install: the Install button was clicked at about 23:19. The permission screen asked to View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. The Install button normally opens a grant tab; in our own tab the install form was sent into the same tab and submitted with a script. The first attempt ended in the message UpsellPlus was not added to your shop because the permission screen was closed too early; the second attempt worked. After the install the product opened at once with the setup line We analyzed your last 60 days of orders. There was no Shopify approval screen and no payment screen. Core action: See my recommended strategies, Offers, Create offer, filter Cart, Smart cross-sell, Use this play opened the offer editor with Where (Cart Drawer, Cart Page, Product Detail Page) and Incentive (None, 5% off, 10% off, Custom); we chose Cart Drawer and 10% off. The preview showed The Inventory Not Tracked Snowboard at $854.95 instead of $949.95 and Gift Card at $9.00 instead of $10.00, each with an Add to Cart button, under the note that real products from the store are shown and that actual products are selected automatically by AI at runtime. A box Place your app block was marked Incomplete: the cart drawer app block still has to be added in the theme. About 4 minutes passed between the install click (23:19) and the first preview (about 23:23), and it took about 6 clicks after the install. Nothing was saved (Discard), nothing was published, the theme was not changed and no order was placed. Plans and billing: this is a development store. Settings, Billing says Development store. You have full access to every feature, free. Development, partner and Shopify staff stores are never charged. It also says that a store on a paid Shopify plan starts on the free plan like any other shop and that pricing then follows the steps below. The page How pricing works says that the price follows the upsell revenue UpsellPlus generates, with nine steps: Basic up to $500 at $49 a month, Pro up to $2,000 at $119, Advanced up to $5,000 at $199, Scale 1 up to $10,000 at $299, Scale 2 up to $15,000 at $399, Scale 3 up to $20,000 at $499, Scale 4 up to $30,000 at $699, Scale 5 up to $40,000 at $799 and Unlimited at $999 a month. All prices are in USD and appear on the Shopify invoice. No Shopify approval screen was reached, nothing was approved. Differences with the dossier and the listing: the app shows the entry step as Basic Plan where the dossier says Launch; the app shows no Free plan among the nine steps although the listing says Free plan available (on a development store the free plan cannot be tested); the listing shows tiers up to $199 while the app shows six more steps up to $999 that are tied to upsell revenue. No price field is changed here. Cancelling: no paid plan exists on a development store, so no cancel route for a plan was seen. Settings, Apps, the menu behind the three dots for UpsellPlus offered Open app, View details and Uninstall (and a help link). The dialog Uninstall UpsellPlus? says that you will no longer be able to use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request is sent to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. It requires a Reason for uninstalling. Not tested: checkout, thank-you page, post-purchase and POS upsells (Plus or paid, the listing says checkout upsells are Plus only), the free plan on a real paid store, A/B tests, analytics with real data, the cart drawer app block, a real order and any shopper data, so we could not tell whether shoppers would take an offer. Clean up: our own tab was used; the offer was not saved and the theme was not changed. UpsellPlus was uninstalled on 17 Nov through Settings, Apps with the reason Testing multiple apps and left the Installed list. Other apps were not touched and our own tab was closed. The price fields are not changed here. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The preview is only a preview: the cart drawer app block still had to be added in the theme, nothing was saved, and we saw no shopper data, so we could not tell whether shoppers would take the offer. The app calls the entry plan Basic where the dossier says Launch, shows no Free plan, and its price follows upsell revenue in nine steps up to $999 a month, while the listing shows tiers only up to $199.
